failure_prob_per_hour.citation: Wiener Gesundheitsverbund medical physics, 'How is downtime defined for our CT?' (service log of one Toshiba/Canon Aquilion LB CT): downtime 22.5, 11.5, 38.5, 0, 14, 0, 0, 0, 4, 3.2, 22.3, 0.3 hours in 2011-2022 against 2,500 operating hours a year (0.0% to 1.5%, mean about 0.4%); vendor guarantees downtime not above 2% a year. Value = 0.4% downtime / 4 h mean repair (this catalog's repair_min).
failure_prob_per_hour.note: DERIVED from a single scanner's log (Austria, radiotherapy-planning CT, weekday 07-17 operation), so weak evidence; high end = the 2% contractual ceiling. No multi-site published CT failure-rate study was found. Keep failure_prob x repair_min/60 between 0.1% and 2% if repair_min is changed.

revenue_per_use.citation: CMS OPPS Addendum B, July 2026 update (national unadjusted payment rate by HCPCS code), wage-adjusted for CCN 310038 as rate x (0.6 x wage index 1.2727 + 0.4) = x1.1636; unweighted mean over 10 common ED CT codes (70450, 70496, 70498, 71250, 71260, 71275, 72125, 74176, 74177, 74178; APCs 5522, 5523, 5571, 5572)
revenue_per_use.note: Unweighted across codes (no ED volume by code was obtained); range = cheapest to dearest of those codes. Status indicators ['Q3']: Q1 services are PACKAGED (no separate payment) when billed on the same claim as an ED visit, Q3 services may be paid as a composite - so this is the stand-alone rate and an upper bound on the marginal Medicare payment during an ED visit. Facility payment only, no radiologist fee.

result_delay_min.citation: Brunner J et al. (2014) The Boston Marathon bombing: after-action review of the Brigham and Women's Hospital emergency radiology response, Radiology 273(1):78-87 (abstract): annual median time from examination completion to available dictated text report 74 min (IQR 35-127) for ED imaging; annual median order-to-completion 72 min (IQR 40-129) for CT and 31 min (IQR 19-48) for radiography.
result_delay_min.note: One US academic Level I trauma centre, 2012-2013; the report figure covers ED radiography and CT together. Clinicians often act on images or a verbal read before the dictated report, so this is an upper-leaning value for decision delay. Order-to-completion includes queueing and patient preparation and is a validation target, not the procedure_min input; another ED measured median 108 min (IQR 57-182) for 5,685 CTs (Dhanik A et al. 2024, West J Emerg Med, https://doi.org/10.5811/westjem.17831).

procedure_min.citation: Vrijsen BEL et al. (2022) Shorter laboratory turnaround time is associated with shorter emergency department length of stay, BMC Emerg Med 22(1):207: 23,718 ED visits, median laboratory turnaround 51.1 min (IQR 41.1-65.0), median time from arrival to testing 7.0 min; the laboratory stage was 69% of turnaround. Hausfater P et al. (2020) Acad Emerg Med 27(10):974-983 (cluster-randomised, 20,923 patients): time to results 79 (SD 34) min with the central laboratory vs 28 (SD 31) with point-of-care testing, ED stay 210 vs 203 min (difference -9 min, 95% CI -22 to 5).
procedure_min.note: DERIVED lognormal: median 51.1 and IQR 41.1-65.0 give sigma 0.34 (cv 0.35) and mean 54. Netherlands (one university hospital) and France (one ED). This is order-to-result turnaround, which is what the Wave 0 comment defined for the lab. Point-of-care testing would cut it to about 28 min but did not significantly shorten the ED stay.
